_comment: The result we expect from each control of the OpenSSF scanner (pvtr-github-repo-scanner), as the weekly run in CI sees it (.github/workflows/pvtr-scan.yml; comparison in scripts/pvtr-scan.ts, `pnpm check:pvtr`). The run fails and posts to the alerts channel only when a control is WORSE than its entry (Passed, then Not Applicable, then Needs Review, then Failed), an entry that is not Passed has expired or lacks a reason or an expiry date, or the scan itself fails. A control with no entry is expected to Pass. An improvement only shows in the job summary: change the entry (to Passed once it passes; delete the reason and expiry). A result list means CI may see either, for a stated reason. The workflow token reads less than an administrator's, so these are CI's results, not the table in docs/checklists/OSPS_BASELINE.md. An expiry is YYYY-MM-DD, at most 12 months out; renew it by re-checking the reason. How to update: docs/trust/THREAT_MODEL.md, Scheduled scanners.

OSPS-AC-03.01.reason: The ruleset requires a pull request and has no bypass actors (docs/checklists/OSPS_BASELINE.md says Met), but the scanner only counts an update rule, a push restriction or a required approval as protection. The workflow token cannot see the branch protection settings an administrator can (rulesets in full), so in CI the scanner cannot tell and reports Needs Review; with an administrator's token, Failed.

OSPS-AC-04.02.reason: The scanner lists every job that has write permissions (auto-merge, the coverage comment) and asks for a human to confirm they are needed; each is limited to the job that needs it (docs/checklists/OSPS_BASELINE.md).

OSPS-BR-01.02.reason: A retired control id; the scanner logs it for visibility only.

OSPS-BR-01.03.reason: The scanner asks for a manual review of main-red-alert.yml, the one workflow_run workflow; it checks out main itself and skips runs from forks (docs/checklists/OSPS_BASELINE.md).
